evidence.claim: Putin approved Russia's nuclear-deterrence doctrine, which remained the governing baseline in 2022 and made the president the overall authority for nuclear deterrence policy and use conditions.
evidence.title: Executive Order Approving the Basic Principles of State Policy of the Russian Federation on Nuclear Deterrence
evidence.publisher: Official Internet Portal of Legal Information
evidence.excerpt: Putin approved Russia's nuclear-deterrence doctrine, which remained the governing baseline in 2022 and made the president the overall authority for nuclear deterrence policy and use conditions.
evidence.source_locator: official publication text and Kremlin summary page
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official legal publication of the presidential decree; the text is the binding baseline in force during 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential act setting the formal nuclear decision framework before 2022
contrary_evidence: The document is a formal baseline, not proof of prudent 2022 conduct.
Later 2022 actions moved the posture in a more dangerous direction.

evidence.claim: Putin authorized the full-scale invasion of Ukraine and said the goal was to demilitarise and 'denazify' Ukraine.
evidence.title: Russia's Putin authorises 'special military operation' against Ukraine
evidence.excerpt: Putin authorized the full-scale invasion of Ukraine and said the goal was to demilitarise and 'denazify' Ukraine.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters report quoting the president directly on the launch decision and justification.
contrary_evidence: The Kremlin framed the operation as defensive.
The report shows the operational choice was still an invasion.

evidence.claim: Russia signaled it was scaling back ambitions in Ukraine to focus on Donbass, saying the first phase was mostly complete.
evidence.title: Russia reframes war goals as Ukrainians advance near Kyiv
evidence.excerpt: Russia signaled it was scaling back ambitions in Ukraine to focus on Donbass, saying the first phase was mostly complete.
evidence.source_locator: lead and quoted statement from the Russian General Staff
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report on a major operational shift announced by Russian defense leadership.
evidence.period_fit: Late March 2022 battlefield and war-aim adjustment
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Putin's state and military leadership
contrary_evidence: Western officials said the original aims were a pretext for overthrowing Ukraine's government.
The shift followed military failure near Kyiv rather than a peace settlement.

evidence.claim: Russia said it would sharply reduce military activity around Kyiv and Chernihiv to increase mutual trust and create conditions for further negotiations.
evidence.title: Russia says it will sharply cut military activity near Kyiv, Chernihiv
evidence.excerpt: Russia said it would sharply reduce military activity around Kyiv and Chernihiv to increase mutual trust and create conditions for further negotiations.
evidence.source_locator: lead paragraph and quoted statement by Deputy Defence Minister Alexander Fomin
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report on an announced operational reduction tied to negotiations.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Russian state action under Putin's authority, but the reduction was tactical rather than a verified peace breakthrough
contrary_evidence: The reduction did not end the war.
Russian forces kept major offensives elsewhere.

evidence.claim: Amnesty concluded that Russian military forces likely deliberately targeted the Mariupol drama theatre despite knowing civilians were sheltering there.
evidence.title: Ukraine: Deadly Mariupol theatre strike 'a clear war crime' by Russian forces – new investigation
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty concluded that Russian military forces likely deliberately targeted the Mariupol drama theatre despite knowing civilians were sheltering there.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Investigation based on survivor interviews and digital evidence, with a clear conclusion on the strike.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Russian military forces under Putin's command
contrary_evidence: Russia denied bombing the theatre.
The evidence presented by Amnesty pointed the other way.

evidence.claim: Russia and Ukraine signed a landmark deal to unblock grain exports from Black Sea ports and ease an international food crisis.
evidence.title: Ukraine and Russia seal grain deal as U.S. pledges more military aid
evidence.excerpt: Russia and Ukraine signed a landmark deal to unblock grain exports from Black Sea ports and ease an international food crisis.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters wire on a major negotiated humanitarian/economic arrangement.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Russian state participation under Putin, though the arrangement was multilateral and brokered by the UN and Turkey
contrary_evidence: The deal did not end the broader war.
Subsequent strikes threatened implementation.

evidence.claim: Putin announced partial mobilization, tied the war to defense of territorial integrity, and said Russia would use all available means, adding that the warning was not bluff.
evidence.title: Address by the President of the Russian Federation
evidence.excerpt: Putin announced partial mobilization, tied the war to defense of territorial integrity, and said Russia would use all available means, adding that the warning was not bluff.
evidence.source_locator: speech transcript paragraphs containing the territorial-integrity and 'not bluff' language
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official Kremlin transcript of a live presidential address with direct attribution.
contrary_evidence: The Kremlin said the warning was defensive.
The speech escalated the war and widened coercive pressure.

evidence.claim: Russian-controlled regions announced referendums on joining Russia after battlefield setbacks, and Reuters described the move as a serious escalation in Moscow's standoff with the West.
evidence.title: Russia triggers plan to formally annex occupied Ukrainian regions
evidence.excerpt: Russian-controlled regions announced referendums on joining Russia after battlefield setbacks, and Reuters described the move as a serious escalation in Moscow's standoff with the West.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters report on the annexation trigger and escalation context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Putin's state and proxy apparatus in occupied Ukrainian territory
contrary_evidence: Russia framed the move as local self-determination.
The votes were widely denounced as coerced and illegitimate.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Putin would host a Kremlin signing ceremony to incorporate four Ukrainian regions, a step toward formally annexing about 15 percent of Ukraine.
evidence.title: Russia's annexation plan in Ukraine: Kremlin signing ceremony
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Putin would host a Kremlin signing ceremony to incorporate four Ukrainian regions, a step toward formally annexing about 15 percent of Ukraine.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters summary of the annexation legal step and Kremlin ceremony.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct personal and state attribution to Putin's annexation decision
contrary_evidence: Russia claimed the regions were joining by referendum.
International actors treated the annexation as illegal seizure.

evidence.claim: Meduza reported that Russia's State Duma ratified treaties on the 'admission' of the DNR, LNR, Zaporizhzhia, and Kherson, formalizing the annexation package Putin had signed.
evidence.title: Госдума единогласно одобрила аннексию оккупированных украинских территорий
evidence.excerpt: Meduza reported that Russia's State Duma ratified treaties on the 'admission' of the DNR, LNR, Zaporizhzhia, and Kherson, formalizing the annexation package Putin had signed.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent Russian-language reporting on the ratification of Putin's annexation treaties.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Putin's treaty-signing and Russia's state apparatus
contrary_evidence: The article itself notes these were occupied Ukrainian territories.
The ratification did not alter international law's rejection of the annexation.

evidence.claim: Meduza's Bucha report described Russian soldiers killing, raping, and torturing residents in a town that had been occupied by Russian forces.
evidence.title: Буча ... репортаж «Медузы» из Бучи — о том, что сейчас происходит в городе, где российские солдаты убивали, насиловали и пытали жителей
evidence.excerpt: Meduza's Bucha report described Russian soldiers killing, raping, and torturing residents in a town that had been occupied by Russian forces.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent Russian-language local reporting with direct post-occupation testimony and reporting.
evidence.period_fit: Post-withdrawal evidence on spring 2022 occupation conduct
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attribution runs through Russian forces under Putin's invasion and occupation order
contrary_evidence: This is journalistic reporting, not a legal judgment.
It is still strong evidence of unlawful conduct in occupied territory.

evidence.claim: The OHCHR report said Russian forces killed at least 441 civilians in the early days of the invasion in areas they controlled.
evidence.title: Russian forces killed hundreds of civilians early in Ukraine war - UN report
evidence.excerpt: The OHCHR report said Russian forces killed at least 441 civilians in the early days of the invasion in areas they controlled.
evidence.source_locator: lead paragraph and quoted UN summary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report summarizing a UN human-rights finding with direct numbers and attribution.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Russian armed forces under Putin's command
contrary_evidence: The report focused on early invaded areas, not the entire war.
Its findings still strongly corroborate unlawful early conduct.

unresolved_gaps: Direct evidence on command-and-control discipline, custody, accident-prevention, and other nuclear safety procedures in 2022 is thin.
Direct evidence on expert governance and risk institutions is weak relative to the rhetoric and escalation evidence.
The package needs better household and distribution evidence, not just macro stabilization and state-budget outcomes.
Direct evidence that appointments and institutions translated into durable productivity investment is still thin.
Direct 2022 delivery evidence for health, education, housing, and food security inside Russia remains thin.
Implementation and take-up by region and group are not well documented.
Direct documentary proof of Putin's personal beneficial ownership, asset control, or hidden conflicts remains limited.
The appointment and accountability map is still too thin for a fully rounded honesty judgment.
Direct 2022 implementation metrics for procurement, output, and battlefield effectiveness remain thin.
The package still needs a cleaner separation between frantic adaptation, temporary stabilization, and genuinely effective goal advancement.
